reasons: Depends on Node being installed and on exact printed wording.

terms.meaning: a Python testing tool that runs functions named test_ and reports whether each one passed
a test written after a bug is fixed, to make sure the bug does not return
a program that runs JavaScript outside a web browser
continuous integration, an automatic checker that runs tests whenever code changes
a named design setting, such as a color or spacing value, that code refers to by name

used_by: The repository's pytest run in continuous integration (described in the file, configuration not in the packet)

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test purpose and file location
sections.what: Explains why these tests exist and finds the validator script in the parent folder. It also imports the testing tools.
sections.why: Likely reason: records the bug these tests guard against, so later readers know why they exist.
sections.watch_out: The validator path is built from this file's location, so moving either file breaks the tests.

sections.name: _run
sections.title: Running the validator on sample CSS
sections.what: Writes a small CSS sample into a temporary folder, runs the validator with Node on that folder, and returns the printed output and exit code. If Node is not installed, the test is skipped.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets each test feed in CSS text and check the result without touching real project files.
sections.watch_out: A skipped test is not a pass, so check the test summary for skips when Node is missing.

sections.name: test_flags_hardcoded_hex_sharing_line_with_token
sections.title: Hardcoded color next to a token is flagged
sections.what: Checks that a hardcoded color written on the same line as a design token is reported and that the validator exits with a failure code.
sections.why: Likely reason: guards against the earlier bug where any line containing a token was ignored.
sections.watch_out: The check looks for the color text in the printed output, so rewording the report can break this test even if the checker still works.

sections.name: test_token_only_line_reports_no_violation
sections.title: Token-only line stays clean
sections.what: Checks that a line using only design tokens produces the clean message and a success exit code, so no false alarms appear.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes sure the fix for the earlier bug did not create false alarms.
sections.watch_out: This test depends on the exact clean message text, so changing that wording will fail it.

summary: Two automated tests that check the token validator flags a hardcoded color on a line that also uses a token, and stays quiet when a line uses only tokens.
purpose: Guards the validator against a past bug returning.
why: The file header says an earlier version skipped any line containing a token. Likely reason: these tests were added so that bug does not come back.
how: 1. Write a sample CSS file into a temporary folder. 2. Run the validator on it with Node. 3. Check the printed text and the exit code. Each test does this once.
inputs: Sample CSS text written by each test.
outputs: A pass, fail, or skip result for each test, reported by pytest.
risks: Only two cases are covered, so most checks are untested. The tests skip when Node is missing, which can hide that gap.
debug: Run pytest in the tests folder with verbose output. A failure message includes the validator's printed output. If tests skip, install Node and run them again.
